questionText: What counts towards the net time of an AI-assisted task?

answerOptions.text: Drafting, review and rework, compared with the baseline
Only the time until the model answers
Only the time spent writing the brief

explanation: Net time counts everything the AI route costs and compares it with the same task without AI.

questionText: What did the 2025 METR study with experienced developers show?

answerOptions.text: They were 19% slower with AI but believed they were faster.

explanation: They expected a 24% gain beforehand, estimated 20% afterwards, and measured 19% slower.

questionText: Which three axes does the course's triage use?
explanation: Frequent, cheap when wrong and quick to check: that is where you start.

questionText: What does the jagged frontier from Dell'Acqua et al. (2023) mean?

answerOptions.text: AI never helps with creative tasks.
Tasks that look similar can lie inside or outside a model's capabilities.

explanation: Inside the frontier AI helped markedly; just outside, participants were 19 percentage points less likely to be correct.

answerOptions.text: Tone, output format and fixed boundaries
Login details for the customer portal

explanation: Persistent only for what applies to every task. Material comes per task, credentials never.

questionText: Why does an overloaded context hurt?

answerOptions.text: Models refuse long texts as a rule.
Information in the middle of long contexts is used less well.
It changes the model's training data.

explanation: Liu et al. (2024): information at the beginning or end is used best, in the middle markedly worse.

questionText: Which combination makes prompt injection especially dangerous?

answerOptions.text: Long emails, short replies, little time
Many users, one model, one password
Private data, untrusted content and a way out
A weak model and a tight budget

explanation: Without one of the three, an injected instruction can no longer leak data. That limits the damage; injection itself cannot be reliably prevented.

questionText: What limits the consequences of a prompt injection most reliably?

answerOptions.text: A system-prompt line telling the model to ignore others' instructions
Least privilege and approval for everything that leaves

explanation: OWASP considers a fool-proof defence unresolved. So limit what can happen in the worst case.

questionText: An answer quotes note A correctly; note B is newer and contradicts it. What is right?

answerOptions.text: Follow the newer note and flag the conflict
Use note A because it was cited

explanation: A correct quote from a stale note is still wrong. Date and version are part of the check.

questionText: What does a citation in an AI answer do?

answerOptions.text: It proves the statement is true.

explanation: A citation invites you to look. Whether the source supports the statement is for you to check.

questionText: What did Magesh et al. (2025) find for legal research tools that use retrieval?

answerOptions.text: Invented or distorted content in 17 to 33% of queries

explanation: Retrieval reduces errors but does not remove them. You check important citations at the source.

answerOptions.text: People monitoring a mostly reliable system miss its rare errors.

explanation: That is why approval needs fixed checks alongside it (Parasuraman and Manzey 2010).

questionText: Which case belongs in the test of a new email workflow?

answerOptions.text: A booby-trapped email with a hidden instruction
Only emails that are sure to work

explanation: A test that cannot fail proves nothing. Prepared cases expose gaps without harm.

questionText: A cloud service is to process personal customer data on your behalf. What do you need first?

answerOptions.text: A data processing agreement under GDPR Art. 28

explanation: First the contract, then the maths, then the test with your own cases.

questionText: What makes a good stop criterion for a pilot?

answerOptions.text: It is set after the pilot.
It is fixed in advance, measurable and dated.

explanation: Only a criterion fixed and measurable in advance stops you from measuring what you want to believe.
